title: BOOM (riscv-boom/riscv-boom) -- LargeBoomV4 on rocket-chip DefaultConfig
_note: BOOM v4's LargeBoom core (the out-of-order fetch / rename / issue / execute /
commit pipeline, its non-blocking D$ with the MSHR file, the TAGE-SC-L and
BIM / BTB predictors and the load-store unit) inside rocket-chip's
DefaultConfig SoC, emitted by firtool as one SystemVerilog file per module --
the same shape as the rocket-chip and XiangShan families.
Why generation is not simply `mill` in the BOOM checkout.  BOOM is a Chisel
LIBRARY with no elaboration target, and three separate things block the
obvious routes, all measured on 2026-10-26:
* Its own build.sc resolves rocketchip / cde / hardfloat / diplomacy as
`1.6-snapshot` ivy artifacts that are NOT published on Maven Central --
`mill boom.compile` fails on all three (chipyard gets them from a local
publishLocal).  So boom_setup.sh compiles BOOM as an extra module INSIDE
the rocket-chip checkout, which this family clones alongside and which the
rocket-chip family already elaborates; mill, firtool 1.162.0 and dtc are
installed by rocket_setup.sh under $ROCKET_TOOLS.
* Only the v4 tree is compiled.  BOOM v3's common/ imports a `pmu` package
(CanHavePMUEvents, PMUParams, PMURegistry, PMUScopeKey, PMUTileLink) that
lives in chipyard and in neither checkout: all 19 errors of a whole-tree
build come from those seven v3 files, while v4 produces only warnings.
* BOOM ships no elaborable config: every core mixin is
`WithNLargeBooms(n: Int = 1)`, and a Scala DEFAULT ARGUMENT is not a
no-argument constructor, so the reflection-based loader behind the
generator's `--config` cannot instantiate one.  boom_harness/boomsweep/
BoomSweepConfigs.scala owns the no-arg wrappers, the way chipyard does,
so the family needs no chipyard checkout.
always_srcs: the two Verilog blackboxes the generated modules instantiate
(plusarg_reader, EICG_wrapper) ship in rocket-chip's src/main/resources/vsrc,
not in the firtool output -- without them read_slang has no reference.
Excluded, as in the rocket-chip family: the TestHarness and its
simulation-only models, the TLMonitor assertion checkers, and the
TestHarness-scale AXI backing memory (mem_33554432x64 / AXI4RAM), which
read_uhdm stops on at RTLIL::WIDTH_LIMIT.
First local sweep 2026-10-27 (422 rows, MEM_LIMIT_KB=7000000 as the nightly
uses): 326 / 422 comparable proven, 418 / 422 elaborate, 379 co-sim PASS,
0 undriven on every row that elaborated, 9.6 h of row time (hence eight
shards).
Open: 68 rows exhaust the SAT budget (48 timeout, 20 over the memory cap),
every one with a clean co-simulation; 4 rows cannot elaborate under the 7 GB
cap at all -- BoomCore, BoomTile, TilePRCIDomain_1 and ExampleRocketSystem,
whose source closures are 64 to 108 MB and which abort in Surelog with
std::bad_alloc, the same whole-core class as BlackParrot; and 24 `differs`
rows of which 23 also diverge in co-simulation with read_slang clean.
Those divergences are ONE reader defect, fixed alongside this manifest: a
block-local declared with an initialiser in a clocked always block
(`automatic logic _GEN = a & b;`, which is how firtool stages every shared
sub-expression of a register update) had its write dropped, so the scoped
wire was undriven and every `x <= _GEN ? a : b` in the block held forever.
DivUnit, ALUExeUnit and BranchKillableQueue were re-measured against the fix
and are proven with a clean co-simulation; the same defect was behind all
four of the rocket-chip family's named open leads (BTB, CSRFile, Frontend,
ITLB).  test/ff_block_local_decl_init is the ratchet.
